title: Sebastian and the Harbor
premise: Ansel Zhou, a pastry chef whose harbor-side café is three missed payments from foreclosure, has sworn off love since a betrayal she still bakes around. When her ex announces an engagement at the family reunion, she recruits Sebastian Hale — a quiet boat restorer who buys her day-old croissants every morning — to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. The fake date turns devastatingly real, but Sebastian is hiding that he's the estranged heir whose family trust is buying out the harbor, including her lease. When Ansel discovers his inheritance is the very thing destroying her café, she must choose between the belonging she's finally found and the identity she's built alone; in the end, Sebastian renounces his claim to the harbor trust, Ansel's community buys the building as a co-op, and the two open the café's doors on a morning where no one has to leave on the last train.
about_author: Wren Dunmore spent a decade working the counter of her grandmother's bakery on a working waterfront before turning to fiction full-time. She writes love stories about people who build things with their hands and guard their hearts with both of them.

chapters.title: Three Payments from Gone
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel counts the café's remaining days while perfecting a plum tart she can't afford the plums for, and notices the quiet boat restorer who buys day-old croissants every morning at closing. Emotional beat: weary tenderness — she's good at feeding people and terrible at letting them feed her.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Her sister calls: the family reunion will celebrate Ansel's ex-fiancé's engagement, and everyone expects her to bring someone or be pitied. On impulse, she asks the croissant man, Sebastian, who hesitates, then says yes. Emotional beat: reckless hope disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They rehearse their story over flour and sawdust — how they met, his job, his family — and the fake details keep sliding into true ones. Ansel learns Sebastian left home years ago and doesn't say why. Emotional beat: the dangerous comfort of pretending.

chapters.title: The Zhou Reunion
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The reunion: her ex's smug engagement toast, her grandmother's sharp eyes, and Sebastian's hand finding hers under the table without prompting. They perform so well that Ansel forgets, for one whole hour, that it's a performance. Emotional beat: belonging, borrowed and intoxicating.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. By dessert, the lie collapses into a real kiss on the porch, witnessed by no one. Sebastian drives home gripping the wheel, knowing what he hasn't told her: his family's trust is the anonymous buyer circling the harbor properties — including her café. Emotional beat: guilt blooming inside joy.

chapters.title: Salt and Sugar
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A giddy week of real dates — boat repairs at dawn, pastry experiments at midnight. Ansel lets him stay past the last train for the first time. Meanwhile, foreclosure letters arrive, and Sebastian quietly stalls the trust's paperwork. Emotional beat: happiness with a crack running through it.

chapters.title: The Name on the Letterhead
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel meets the trust's lawyer and sees Sebastian's family name on the acquisition documents — then finds Sebastian's signature on the original offer for her building. She throws him out before he can explain. Emotional beat: betrayal layered over betrayal; the past tense snaps shut.

chapters.title: What He Inherited
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian confronts his father, who offers him the trust's chair — everything he was raised to want — if he closes the harbor deal. Instead Sebastian digs up the trust's charter and finds a clause: a beneficiary can contest an acquisition that displaces an existing tenant. Emotional beat: choosing inheritance of character over inheritance of capital.

chapters.title: The Harbor Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the public hearing on the harbor buyout, Sebastian testifies against his own family and invokes the tenant clause, while Ansel, not knowing, speaks for her café with the whole neighborhood behind her. Their eyes meet across the room. Emotional beat: public vulnerability; two truths colliding into one fight.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The co-op purchase succeeds with Sebastian's contested vote as the deciding margin; he renounces his trust seat. He shows up at closing with flour on his sleeves and asks to stay — not past the last train, but past the part where leaving is an option. She says yes. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; identity kept and shared.
